proposals.before: Soon afterward he asked to step down and was appointed Supernumerary.
proposals.after: Soon afterward he asked to step down and was appointed Specially Advanced.
proposals.reason: 特進 is the honorary title Specially Advanced, not Supernumerary (which this chapter already uses for 給事中).

proposals.before: Shortly thereafter he requested to yield his position and was appointed Supernumerary.
proposals.after: Shortly thereafter he requested to yield his position and was appointed Specially Advanced.
proposals.reason: 特進 should be rendered Specially Advanced, not Supernumerary.

proposals.after: All extant editions now read "Specially Advanced."
proposals.reason: The quoted office is 特進 (Specially Advanced), not Supernumerary.

proposals.after: Now all editions uniformly read "Specially Advanced."
proposals.reason: The quoted office is 特進 (Specially Advanced), not Supernumerary.

proposals.before: 〈At that time Chen Shou and Chen Ye were appointed to supervise; Right Remonstrator and Direct Historian of the History Office Zhang Guan and others carried out the collation.
proposals.after: 〈At that time Ministers Shou and Ye were appointed to supervise; Right Remonstrator and Direct Historian of the History Office Zhang Guan and others carried out the collation.
proposals.reason: 臣綬、臣燁 uses 臣 as the memorial self-reference “minister/your servant,” not the surname Chen; the literal already has Ministers Shou and Ye.

decisions.reason: s0017 has 拜特進; 特進 is the Tang honorary title Specially Advanced. Rendering it as Supernumerary invents a different office and conflicts with the chapter’s own use of that English for other titles.
The literal’s appointment phrase matches 拜特進; Specially Advanced is the correct rendering of 特進, whereas Supernumerary is a different office title.
s0018 says 今諸本並云特進, quoting the office-name 特進; the English quote must read Specially Advanced, not Supernumerary.
The literal likewise quotes 特進 from 並云特進; replacing Supernumerary with Specially Advanced restores the correct office name in the quotation.
臣綬、臣燁 uses 臣 as the memorial self-reference “minister/your servant,” not the surname Chen; Ministers Shou and Ye matches the Chinese and the existing literal.

claimRetractions.reason: The alternate name Chen Shou was created only by misreading 臣 as the surname Chen; s0037 supports the given name 綬 (Shou) with 臣 as a ministerial self-reference, not a Chen surname.
The alternate name Chen Ye was created only by misreading 臣 as the surname Chen; s0037 supports the given name 燁 (Ye) with 臣 as a ministerial self-reference, not a Chen surname.
